story.head: Stay out of the box, Sabres
paras: The Sabres have won three straight, while the Golden Knights (9-5-1) lost 5-2 to New Jersey on Oct 30. Going in, the Knights are second in the Pacific (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Sabres seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 13th).

The Golden Knights have played better than their record (.633) says: their chances are worth about .691, and their goaltending has held them back. The Sabres’ record (.607) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.540), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Golden Knights draw more penalties than they take (1st) and have the league’s best penalty kill (1st), but have had shaky goaltending (31st). As for the Sabres, they rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd), but don't block many shots (29th). The Golden Knights’ power play (4th) could do real damage against the Sabres’ penalty kill (22nd), and the Golden Knights have the edge over the Sabres on preventing dangerous shots.

Jack Eichel (7 G / 13 A / 20 P in 15 GP) leads the Golden Knights in scoring, and Mark Stone (9 G / 8 A / 17 P in 15 GP) has a team-high nine goals. For the Sabres, Tage Thompson (10 G / 7 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jack Quinn (8 G / 6 A / 14 P in 14 GP) isn’t far behind.

Adin Hill (5-2-0 / .891 SV% in 7 GS) will likely start for Vegas. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (4-3-3 / .873 SV% in 9 GS) and Colten Ellis (3-1-0 / .880 SV% in 5 GS). Luukkonen has started six of their last ten games, including the last one on Oct 31. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

items.text: The Sabres are newly without Konsta Helenius, have been without Jiří Kulich since Oct 21, and have had to make do without Alex Lyon and Conor Timmins all season.
The Golden Knights have been without Parker Wotherspoon and Victor Olofsson for several games.
Zach Benson has one goal on chances worth about 5.0 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Mitch Marner has a point in nine straight games.
